title: Neighbours
wiki_lead:
Neighbours  is an Australian television soap opera that aired from 1985 to 2025. It was created by television executive Reg Watson. The Seven Network commissioned the show following the success of Watson's earlier soap Sons and Daughters. Although successful in Melbourne, Neighbours underperformed in the Sydney market and was cancelled by Seven Network four months after it began airing. It was immediately commissioned by rival Network Ten for a second production season, which began screening in January 1986. Neighbours became the longest-running drama series in Australian television history in 1997, and was inducted into the Logie Hall of Fame in 2005.
The storylines concern the lives of the people who live and work in Erinsborough, a fictional suburb of Melbourne, Victoria. The series centres on the residents of Ramsay Street, a dead end street, and its neighbouring area, the Lassiters complex, which includes a bar, hotel, café, police station, lawyers' office and park. Neighbours began with a focus on three households created by Watson – including the Ramsay and Robinson families, who have a long history and an ongoing rivalry. Over the serial's early years, three additional houses on the street were introduced as regular settings. Pin Oak Court, in Vermont South, is the real cul-de-sac that doubled for Ramsay Street. The houses featured are real and the residents allowed the production to shoot external scenes in their yards. The interior scenes were filmed at the FremantleMedia studios in Forest Hill.
Until 2022, Neighbours was screened in Australia as a 22-minute episode on weeknights. It moved to Ten's digital channel, Eleven (later rebranded 10 Peach) in January 2011, and was broadcast each weeknight. The show was produced by Fremantle Australia and has been sold to more than sixty countries around the world, making it one of Australia's most successful media exports. Neighbours had been especially successful in the United Kingdom, where it was first screened in October 1986 on BBC One, and achieved huge popularity among British audiences in the late 1980s and 1990s. In 2008, it moved in the UK to Channel 5, which largely funded the series as it was no longer commercially viable for Ten to fund it alone; the show became the first Australian drama to air all year round.
The show was cancelled in early 2022, and the finale was broadcast in July. In November 2022, Amazon Freevee and Fremantle agreed to restart the series, which returned to Network 10 on a permanent basis. Regular production resumed in April 2023 and the show returned in September. The series was cancelled again in February 2025, with production concluding in July and the final episode airing in December.

grok_lead: Neighbours is an Australian soap opera created by Reg Watson for Grundy Television, first broadcast on 18 March 1985 on the Seven Network before moving to Network Ten in 1986 after an initial short run. The series centres on the interconnected lives of residents in the fictional Ramsay Street, a cul-de-sac in the Melbourne suburb of Erinsborough, exploring themes of family, relationships, and community dynamics through daily dramas. Over its nearly 40-year span, it produced more than 8,900 episodes, establishing itself as Australia's longest-running drama series and achieving significant international export success, particularly in the United Kingdom where it garnered peak audiences of over 20 million viewers in the late 1980s and early 1990s. The programme launched the careers of numerous actors who transitioned to global stardom, including Kylie Minogue, Jason Donovan, and Guy Pearce, contributing to its cultural impact beyond Australia. It received widespread acclaim for its accessible storytelling and was inducted into Australia 's Logie Hall of Fame in 2005, reflecting its enduring influence on television production and viewer engagement. Following a cancellation in 2022 due to funding cuts from UK broadcaster Channel 5, Neighbours was revived by Amazon Prime Video for two additional years, with production wrapping in July 2025 and final episodes scheduled to air until December 2025. Despite its popularity, the series faced criticisms, including allegations of racism on set reported by Indigenous actors in 2021, which prompted investigations and highlighted issues of ethnic diversity in its casting. Early storylines were also critiqued for limited representation of non-white characters, though later efforts introduced more diverse roles in response. These incidents underscore tensions between the show's progressive narrative elements and real-world production challenges.
